title: Literature
tagline: Read the great works closely, and learn to say something true and new about them.
overview:
The Certificate in Literature is a three-year course of study in reading, interpreting, and writing about literature. You begin with the fundamentals of close reading across poetry, fiction, and drama, then survey British, American, and ancient literature to build a sense of the traditions writers work within and against.

The core takes you through Shakespeare, Romanticism, the Victorian novel, modernism, African American and postcolonial writing, and literary theory. In your final year you choose a concentration in British, American, or world and comparative literature, and write a senior thesis of literary criticism.
outcomes: Read literary texts closely, attending to language, form, and structure.
Situate works within their historical, cultural, and literary contexts.
Apply major critical and theoretical approaches to interpretation.
Compare works across periods, genres, and traditions, including literature in translation.
Conduct literary research and engage critically with scholarship.
Write clear, original, well-supported arguments about literature.
